content.text:
The drawing shows three parts joined in a chain:

1. **Benzamide:** a benzene ring carrying an ethoxy group (OCH2CH3) ortho to a C(=O)NH amide.
2. **Linker and oxazole:** the amide N is attached to a CH2, which is bonded to C4 of an oxazole ring. In the ring, O1 is at the top right, C2 is bonded to the aryl group, N3 is at the bottom, C4 carries the CH2, and C5 is the CH next to O1.
3. **Aryl group:** a benzene ring attached at oxazole C2. Counting from the attachment point as position 1, it has an isopropoxy group at position 3 and a difluoromethoxy group (OCHF2) at position 4.

Written as SMILES, the benzamide part is CCOc1ccccc1C(=O)NC. The oxazole continues as c1coc(n1)-, and the aryl group is c1ccc(OC(F)F)c(OC(C)C)c1.

Checking the oxazole ring closure: the ring is c1(CH2)coc(Ar)n1, so C4 is bonded to C5 (the CH), C5 to O, O to C2, C2 to N, and N back to C4. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCOc1ccccc1C(=O)NCc1coc(n1)-c1ccc(OC(F)F)c(OC(C)C)c1
